subject: Re: OrbitBio MSA - indemnity limits & evidence for IP claims
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@orbitbio.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Fletcher <mark.fletcher@orbitbio.com>, OrbitBio Contracts <contracts@orbitbio.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: OrbitBio MSA - proposed indemnity limits by module and evidence ask

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team returned the MSA redlines and they flagged two items we need clarified before procurement can sign:

1) Per-module liability cap: OrbitBio is asking that indemnity for third-party IP claims be capped on a per-module basis (e.g., Search module $X, Embeddings module $Y) rather than a single account-level cap. The rationale is that modules will be purchased/pushed to different BU P&Ls.

2) Evidence / escrow trigger: for any IP claim tied to model output, we need a reproducible artifact and would prefer that Redwood provide demo-call logs (or equivalent request/response traces) as proof. OrbitBio wants an explicit escrow-trigger mechanism tied to a threshold (suggested $250k) and a list of acceptable artifacts.

3) Third-party training-data carveout: they want explicit language excluding claims that arise from third-party licensed models or training datasets that were not provided by Redwood.

Attached is our redline (OrbitBio_MSA_Redline_20261212.docx) and a zip of representative demo logs. Appreciate a quick confirmation of feasibility and any proposed counter-language by tomorrow — procurement is on a tight schedule.

Samantha
Samantha Lowe
Sr. Counsel, Procurement
OrbitBio

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-13T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: OrbitBio MSA - proposed indemnity limits by module and evidence ask

All,

Quick legal read:

- Per-module caps: We prefer a single account-level cap (simpler for insurance and carveouts). If OrbitBio insists on module-level splits, propose a hybrid approach — an overall account cap (e.g., $5M) with optional module-level subcaps only where modules are separately ordered under distinct order forms that reference the MSA explicitly. That keeps our overall exposure bounded while giving their BU visibility.

- Demo logs as proof: acceptable in principle if logs are limited to request/response traces and redacted for customer data. We should require a signed attestation from OrbitBio stating the logs reproduce the output at issue and include a signed chain-of-custody for the excerpt used. Also negotiate a narrow evidence window (retain only last 90 days by default).

- Third-party training-data carveout: we can accept a carveout for documented third-party models or datasets that Redwood did not curate or supply, but not for models that OrbitBio fine-tuned on Redwood-hosted artifacts. Clause to propose: "Claims arising solely from Licensed Third-Party Models or Data not provided by Redwood are excluded from Redwood's indemnity obligations, provided the customer supplies verifiable provenance."

- Escrow trigger: $250k is low given our existing attach-rate and insurance layer. Recommend $500k as trigger for escrow/forensics handover; below that we propose remediation-first (patch / model rollback / credits).

I'll attach a one-page redline with proposed language for the MSA and a suggested escalation flow. Ben, Olga — if you approve, I’ll send this to OrbitBio as a clean counter and suggest a 48-hour turnaround.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_MSA_Counter_20261213.docx]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-13T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: OrbitBio MSA - proposed indemnity limits by module and evidence ask

Kimberly / team,

I reviewed the demo-call-logs.zip. High-level tech notes:

- The provided archive contains request/response pairs and some raw prompt text. There are customer identifiers in a few traces; we can sanitize those but need OrbitBio sign-off to alter their forensic artifacts.

- We can produce three artifact types: (1) raw traces (if we get an NDA addendum and written consent), (2) sanitized traces with stable hashing (we replace identifiers with deterministic tokens), or (3) a signed attestation + hash summary that confirms the output was generated by our service at the indicated timestamp. Option 3 is quickest and least risky from a privacy standpoint.

- Storage/retention: our default retention for request traces is 90 days for hosted customers. We can commit to preserve specific, claim-related snapshots longer (escrow) once the mutually-agreed trigger fires and we’ve executed an evidence-preservation SLA.

- Technical feasibility of per-module evidence: technically fine, but evidence must reference the exact model variant and model config (quantization, tokenizer, prompt template). That needs to be recorded in the order form for each module if OrbitBio wants module-level proof.

Recommend: accept sanitized traces + signed attestation as primary acceptable evidence; require escrow-only for full raw traces after a $500k trigger and a forensic request.

—David
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@orbitbio.com>, OrbitBio Contracts <contracts@orbitbio.com>, Mark Fletcher <mark.fletcher@orbitbio.com>

Date: 2026-12-13T14:07:00-08:00
Subject: RE: OrbitBio MSA - indemnity limits & evidence for IP claims (Redwood consolidated counter)

Samantha / OrbitBio team — thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Below is Redwood's consolidated counter-proposal to accelerate procurement: 

1) Liability caps: Redwood proposes an account-level indemnity cap of $4,000,000 (per MSA) that applies across modules. For modules that OrbitBio elects to buy under separate Order Forms and distinct SOWs, we will include optional module subcaps that are capped at the lesser of the module price x 3 or $1,250,000. This hybrid preserves an overall insurance boundary while giving the BU-level accounting OrbitBio requested.

2) Evidence & escrow trigger: Redwood will accept sanitized request/response traces plus a signed attestation as sufficient initial evidence for claim triage. Full raw traces will be produced to OrbitBio only after an escrow trigger of $500,000 is met and a forensic preservation request is executed. We will retain request traces for 90 days by default and will preserve a claim-specific snapshot when the trigger is met. 

3) Third-party training-data carveout: Redwood will accept exclusion language for documented third-party models/datasets not provided by Redwood; however, claims tied to outputs of models that were (a) supplied by Redwood, (b) fine-tuned on Redwood-managed data, or (c) used in conjunction with Redwood-hosted secret keys are not eligible for the carveout. Liberty to require provenance information from OrbitBio.

4) Operational items: Redwood will provide a short forensics intake checklist and a redline that defines acceptable artifacts (sanitized traces, attestations, model variant metadata). The parties agree to a 48-hour turnaround for initial triage response after an evidence submission.

5) Timeline: we request OrbitBio feedback on the counter by 48 hours. If acceptable, Ben will circulate a narrow order form amendment example showing the module subcap math.

Please let me know if you want a short call to finalize language — happy to set up.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
